item.text: I’ve confirmed this is a very small workspace, so I’m reading the app entrypoint and the test harness next to see how much of the command model already exists and where pipeline support should live.

I’ve got the current shape: the app already parses a single command, but the execution model is still “one command or aggregate returns immediately.” I’m now tightening the parser and executor so row-producing commands can chain, while aggregates correctly terminate the pipeline.

I’ve got the implementation plan: parse `|` as a pipeline separator, keep accepting the existing tokenized form, and switch execution to a typed pipeline state so row tables and scalar aggregates are enforced at runtime instead of being special-cased away during parse. After that I’ll add an end-to-end pipeline test and a “scalar result blocks later row commands” test.
The parser needs one more pass: `where` and `distinct` have to stop at `|` too, otherwise a literal pipe gets swallowed into the expression text. I’m fixing that and then I’ll add the pipeline tests.

The runtime change is in place. I’m adding targeted coverage now for the new pipeline syntax and the aggregate-terminal rule so the intended behavior is locked down instead of only inferred from the parser.

item.text: The suite passed end-to-end. I’m pulling exact line references for the parser/executor change and the new regression tests so I can summarize the implementation precisely.

Implemented pipeline composition in the CLI parser and executor.

- `Program.cs` now accepts `|` as a pipeline separator, keeps the existing tokenized command style working, and evaluates commands left to right. See [Program.cs](/tmp/codex-implement-10.hEBxIh/project/Program.cs#L38).
- Execution now tracks result shape explicitly, so row commands operate on tables and aggregates collapse to scalars. Any later row-based command after `count` or `sum` now fails with an error instead of silently misbehaving. See [Program.cs](/tmp/codex-implement-10.hEBxIh/project/Program.cs#L220).
- `groupby` still produces a table, so it can continue through later row commands where meaningful. See [Program.cs](/tmp/codex-implement-10.hEBxIh/project/Program.cs#L247).
- Usage text now reflects pipeline syntax. See [Program.cs](/tmp/codex-implement-10.hEBxIh/project/Program.cs#L634).

Tests added:
- End-to-end pipeline: `where age>30 | sort age | head 3`
- Aggregate terminal behavior: `where ... | count | head 1` now fails
